rules.name: Vector space closure under addition and scalar multiplication
rules.input_form: u, v in V and c in F
rules.output_form: u+v in V and cu in V
preconditions: V is claimed to be a vector space over F
rules.operation: Use the closure axioms to keep vector addition and scalar multiplication inside the space.
examples: In R^n, vector addition and scalar multiplication stay in R^n
counterexamples: A set not closed under these operations is not a vector space under the claimed operations

rules.name: Linear combination formation
preconditions: Each ci is a scalar and each vi is a vector in the same vector space
rules.operation: Form a linear combination of listed vectors with field scalars.
examples: 2v1 - 3v2 + v3 is a linear combination of v1, v2, v3
counterexamples: Using nonlinear operations such as v1*v2 is not a linear combination

rules.name: Span definition
rules.output_form: all linear combinations of vectors in S
rules.operation: Interpret the span of a set as the total collection of its linear combinations.
examples: Span of a nonzero vector in R^2 is a line through the origin
counterexamples: Omitting some allowed scalar combinations gives only part of the span

rules.name: Linear independence criterion
rules.operation: Classify a vector family as linearly independent exactly when the zero combination has only the trivial coefficient solution.
examples: Standard basis vectors in R^n are linearly independent
counterexamples: If one vector is a scalar multiple of another, the pair is dependent

rules.name: Basis criterion
preconditions: The ambient vector space is fixed
rules.operation: Recognize a basis by simultaneous spanning and linear independence.
examples: The standard coordinate vectors form a basis of R^n
counterexamples: A spanning set with redundancy is not automatically a basis

rules.name: Dimension as basis cardinality
preconditions: The vector space is finite-dimensional
rules.operation: Use basis size as the invariant dimension of a finite-dimensional vector space.
examples: Every basis of R^3 has three vectors
counterexamples: Claiming two finite bases of the same vector space have different sizes is invalid

rules.name: Linear transformation preservation rule
preconditions: T is claimed to be linear
rules.operation: Use the defining preservation laws of a linear transformation.
examples: Matrix multiplication by a fixed matrix defines a linear map
counterexamples: T(v) = v + b with nonzero fixed b is not linear

rules.name: Kernel and image definitions
rules.operation: Interpret the kernel as vectors mapped to zero and the image as actual outputs.
examples: The kernel of the zero map is the whole domain
counterexamples: Confusing kernel vectors with output vectors is invalid

rules.name: Rank-nullity pattern
preconditions: The domain is finite-dimensional
rules.operation: Relate domain dimension to image dimension and kernel dimension.
examples: A map from R^4 with rank 3 has nullity 1
counterexamples: Subtracting image dimension from codomain dimension instead of domain dimension is invalid

rules.name: Eigenpair definition
rules.operation: Recognize an eigenpair from scalar-rescaling behavior under a linear map.
examples: For a diagonal matrix, diagonal entries act as eigenvalues on standard basis vectors
counterexamples: The zero vector cannot serve as an eigenvector

rules.name: Inner product positivity and symmetry
rules.output_form: positive and symmetric or conjugate-symmetric pairing
preconditions: An inner product structure is fixed
rules.operation: Use positivity and symmetry axioms of an inner product.
examples: Standard dot product on R^n has these properties
counterexamples: A bilinear form with <v,v> negative for some nonzero v is not an inner product

rules.name: Orthogonality criterion
preconditions: An inner product structure is fixed
rules.operation: Classify vectors as orthogonal when their inner product is zero.
examples: Standard basis vectors in R^n are orthogonal under the dot product
counterexamples: Nonzero angle alone without the inner-product-zero condition is insufficient

rules.name: Projection onto a unit vector
rules.input_form: vector v and unit vector u
preconditions: u is a unit vector under the active inner product
rules.operation: Project a vector orthogonally onto the one-dimensional subspace spanned by a unit vector.
examples: Projecting onto a coordinate axis extracts the matching component under the standard dot product
counterexamples: Omitting unit normalization when the formula requires it is invalid

rules.name: Diagonalization criterion
preconditions: A basis of eigenvectors exists over the active field
rules.operation: Recognize diagonalizability from the existence of a full eigenbasis.
examples: A matrix with n linearly independent eigenvectors is diagonalizable over the active field
counterexamples: Having repeated eigenvalues alone does not prevent or guarantee diagonalization

rules.name: Spectral theorem pattern
preconditions: The matrix is real and symmetric
rules.operation: Apply the spectral theorem to obtain orthogonal diagonalization.
examples: Symmetric matrices can be diagonalized by an orthogonal change of basis
counterexamples: Applying the real symmetric spectral theorem to arbitrary nonsymmetric matrices is invalid

rules.name: Tensor product bilinearity seed rule
preconditions: Tensor product context is fixed
rules.operation: Distribute tensor product over addition in each slot.
examples: Tensor expressions distribute over addition in each slot
counterexamples: Treating tensor product as commutative by default is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid

rules.name: Composition rule expansion

preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Compose structured objects when composition preconditions are satisfied.
examples: Function and operator compositions require compatible codomain-domain interfaces

rules.name: Inverse admissibility expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Introduce inverses only when invertibility conditions are explicitly satisfied.
examples: Matrix inversion requires nonsingularity

rules.name: Constraint propagation expansion

rules.name: Boundary condition integration expansion

rules.name: Conservation tracking expansion
rules.input_form: model evolution with candidate conserved quantity Q

rules.name: Approximation error budget expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Attach explicit error bounds or estimates to approximation-driven outputs.
examples: Numerical approximations should report residual or tolerance-constrained error
counterexamples: Reporting approximations without any error control is invalid

rules.name: Parameter sensitivity expansion
rules.input_form: model output O(theta) with parameter vector theta
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata

examples: Small parameter shifts can cause large output changes near bifurcation or instability regions
